These expand evidence about robustness and applicability; relocating the existing FDR plots is a separate presentation change.
descriptions.E5: Both versions report 500 repetitions for the main simulations and 500 random splits for the clinical analysis, whose error-bar display is retained. The new sensitivity tables use the same 500-repetition averaging practice. No new seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is introduced.
descriptions.E6: Figure 9 newly shows SCORE+-LORD and SCORE+-SAFFRON reaching FDR approximately 0.077 and 0.065 against a 0.05 target under the stress scenario. Tables 2–3 add sensitivity results and power ratios. Main simulation curves have small numerical updates while preserving their ordering; Table 1's yeast counts and the earlier AR(1) and clinical plots are unchanged.
descriptions.T1: Appendix C adds a limited formal generalization: discounted discovery counts, memory-FDR estimators, a predictable-denominator derivation, and a corresponding CPQD requirement for retroactive accounting. The core theorems remain unchanged. The rewritten independence/PQD proof preserves its existing argument, and the memory extension is not presented as a fully proved new theorem.
descriptions.C1: The abstract and introduction retain the same dominance and finite-sample FDR contributions. The conclusion newly asserts compatibility with decaying-memory FDR, supported by Appendix C's outline. Section 2 also removes the stronger phrase 'regardless of the stopping time' from the stated control objective.
descriptions.C2: V2 adds specific qualifications about limited gains with uniformly weak or very strong evidence, interprets the CPQD-violating failure scenario, and explains why shared clinical calibration data do not automatically justify SCORE+. These clarify applicability boundaries without replacing the central interpretation of overshoot refunds.
descriptions.D1: Appendix B.2 supplies an explicit construction recipe for the new stress stream. V2 also adds a direct clinical-dataset access URL to the Golovenkin et al. reference. Existing implementation parameters and data-processing descriptions are largely retained.
descriptions.R1: The cited-work set is retained. Section 4.4 adds explicit positioning of e-LOND, e-LORD, and e-SAFFRON as canonical available procedures and characterizes SCORE's applicability through the standard indicator bound. Appendix C additionally connects the extension directly to Ramdas et al.'s decaying-memory criterion.
descriptions.P1: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. V2 adds a p-value/e-value calibration explanation, refines the CPQD discussion and one proof, and adds publication disclosures. References move before the appendices, while the former Appendices B–D become D–F following the inserted material.
descriptions.P2: V2 adopts a two-column conference main text and extensively reorganizes the simulation displays. Combined plots become family-specific power and power-ratio figures, with FDR trajectories displayed separately in the appendix. A stress-test figure and two sensitivity tables are added; earlier appendix charts are retained and relocated.

P-D13BCBA973.title: YouTube-Occ: Learning Indoor 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction from YouTube Videos

descriptions.M1: v1 back-projects pixels into voxels and contrasts pooled superpixel/supervoxel features. v2 replaces this correspondence mechanism with voxel-anchored Gaussian rendering into the image plane and adds an online class-prototype memory bank and cross-scene contrastive loss. These change the pre-training procedure and objective.
descriptions.E1: Both versions use NYUv2, Occ-ScanNet and YouTube-Occ for indoor semantic occupancy prediction. The larger Internet-video collection, additional architectures and revised label fractions change experimental settings without establishing a new domain, population or task.
descriptions.E2: The NYUv2 comparison adds ISO and EmbodiedOcc; the Occ-ScanNet comparison adds EmbodiedOcc++ and RoboOcc. v2 Table 4 additionally evaluates HASSC, GaussRender and Pri3D against the proposed training strategy, broadening v1's architecture and random-initialization comparisons.
descriptions.E3: YouTube-Occ grows from 14,592 to 100,372 frames, with a new 50K-subset comparison. Pre-training is evaluated on three architectures instead of only Symphonies. The stated pre-training learning rate changes from 8e-4 to 2e-4, and Occ-ScanNet/YouTube-Occ training changes from 30 to 10 epochs. v2 also adds pseudo-label and joint-training controls and revises the evaluated label fractions.
descriptions.E4: Beyond v1's annotation-efficiency and qualitative analyses, v2 adds pseudo-label quality and naive-supervision diagnostics, a 50K-versus-full-data scaling analysis, and component ablations. Tables 5–6 isolate the two losses and test projection choices, learnable Gaussian parameters, prototype momentum and semantic thresholding.
descriptions.E5: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates or significance tests. v1 explicitly acknowledges 'No error bars' in its checklist; that acknowledgment disappears, but v2 retains the same point-estimate reporting practice.
descriptions.E6: The main proposed-method NYUv2 result changes from 30.74/51.12 to 31.65/52.15 mIoU/IoU. Occ-ScanNet changes from 58.15/67.75 to 49.38/61.25, while its Symphonies baseline also changes from 57.85/67.50 to 47.71/59.89. Numerous architecture, scaling, strategy and ablation results are added, and the NYUv2 zero-shot result is removed. These are revised results under changed methods/settings, not controlled cross-version performance gains or losses.
descriptions.T1: v2 adds mathematical definitions for class prototypes, the prototype contrastive loss and the combined objective in Equations 3–4. The region loss retains the earlier contrastive form. This is a limited extension of the formal objectives; no theorem, proof or theoretical guarantee is introduced.
descriptions.C1: v1's abstract claims state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on both benchmarks; v2 instead emphasizes consistent pre-training gains across architectures, especially with limited labels. The methodological contribution is redefined around Gaussian rendering and prototype alignment, and the failure of naive pseudo-label supervision becomes a central claim. The Internet-video occupancy novelty claim remains.
descriptions.C2: v2 introduces geometric-scale and semantic-taxonomy mismatch as conjectured explanations for weak pseudo-label supervision, and interprets the new alignment mechanisms as addressing noisy supervision. Its limitations now include invisible/occluded voxels, extension to temporal or multi-view networks, and dependence on the wall-height assumption. v1 mainly emphasized object-level grouping and identified dynamic/static separation as future work.
descriptions.D1: v2 adds class-name prompting instructions, Gaussian parameterization details and the default prototype momentum of 0.999. It promises public code and data, whereas v1 withheld the dataset and promised code upon acceptance; actual release is not established. Conversely, v1's explicit YouTube train/validation counts and Occ-ScanNet scene-disjoint resplitting description are omitted.
descriptions.R1: New Section 4.3 explicitly distinguishes the approach from GaussTR, AGO, AutoOcc and other outdoor self-supervised methods through calibration assumptions and architectural coupling. References and discussion also expand to alternative training strategies and the manual occupancy-annotation pipeline, while v1's CrossPoint/MM-Point discussion disappears. This materially revises research positioning.
descriptions.P1: The abstract, introduction and related work are extensively rewritten. The narrative now develops manual annotation, automated curation and pseudo-label failure before presenting the revised framework; experiments are reorganized around pipeline evaluation, pre-training and ablations. The checklist is removed, and authorship, affiliations and acknowledgments are updated.
descriptions.P2: The document adopts a different layout and restructures its displays. Figures 1–2 are retained with resizing/relocation, and v1 Figure 4 becomes v2 Figure 5. The NYUv2 qualitative figure and radar plots disappear; new framework and pseudo-label figures appear. Benchmark and few-shot displays are consolidated, with new strategy and ablation tables.

P-2AD752EED0.title: MMD Guidance: Training-Free Distribution Adaptation for Diffusion Models via Maximum Mean Discrepancy Guidance

descriptions.M1: The MMD objective, sampling updates, latent encoding, product-kernel conditioning, and Algorithms 1-2 remain unchanged. Restricting guidance to the final 30 steps is evaluated as a schedule ablation of the existing method.
descriptions.E1: v2 adds synthetic GMM scenarios with widely separated clusters and shifted target centers (Table 5 and Figure 16). Existing image datasets, conditional-generation tasks, and painting-style adaptation remain covered; the painting experiment already appeared in v1.
descriptions.E2: The comparator sets in retained experiments are unchanged. Domain Guidance already appears in v1 Table 1, despite receiving a new discussion paragraph in v2. The larger-reference GMM experiment reuses the existing fine-tuning and unguided comparators.
descriptions.E3: Existing benchmark settings largely persist, but v2 adds experimental designs: component-removal controls, 3,000-point GMM reference sets, and final-30-step versus full guidance. It also describes gradient-error evaluation against a 10,000-reference approximation, averaged over 1,000 generated samples. These are added protocols, not established reruns of the original comparisons.
descriptions.E4: v2 adds diversity-term ablations on GMMs and FFHQ (Tables 18-19), domain-gap robustness tests, larger-reference fine-tuning comparisons, and late-step guidance analysis with generation trajectories. These expand investigation of component necessity, applicability, and guidance timing beyond v1's retained kernel, reference-size, and noisy-reference analyses.
descriptions.E5: v2 removes uncertainty entries from main Table 1. Appendix Table 7 preserves them for MMD, user-trained models, and fine-tuning, but not the FFHQ unguided, CG, or Domain Guidance rows. Both versions retain the five-seed averaging statement and uncertainty reporting in other benchmark tables.
descriptions.E6: Tables 5, 16, 18-20, and 22 add quantitative evidence. For example, Table 19 newly reports sunglasses FD of 941.49 with the cross term alone versus 692.87 with full MMD; Table 22 adds late-step FD of 1732.23. Most earlier benchmark results persist, while selected RRKE entries, runtime sample-count entries, and qualitative examples are removed.
descriptions.T1: The pointwise, uniform, and product-kernel concentration results, assumptions, and Appendix A proofs are retained under new numbering. The omitted Gaussian-specific MMD-gradient display specializes the retained general gradient; its underlying Gaussian derivative remains in Appendix A.2.
descriptions.C1: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: training-free distribution matching through MMD gradients, prompt-aware product kernels, and efficient latent-space implementation. The additional experiments support these claims without materially redefining their scope.
descriptions.C2: v2 adds interpretations that larger domain gaps require stronger guidance and more references, later denoising stages are especially important, and MMD remains competitive when fine-tuning has sufficient data. Existing sparse-reference and kernel-choice limitations remain; the new Impact Statement also discusses dependence on reference-data biases.
descriptions.D1: The v2 abstract newly provides a project-code repository link. Added experiments disclose reference counts and guidance intervals, while existing implementation information, including kernel choices, guidance-scale ranges, encoders, and timing hardware, is largely retained.
descriptions.R1: Section 2 broadens related-work coverage with RKE/Vendi-based diversity guidance and kernel-based online model selection, embedding alignment, and generative-model comparison. This expands the research context beyond the retained discussion of adaptation and MMD training losses, rather than merely updating citation formatting.
descriptions.P1: Most existing prose and the section sequence remain recognizable. Changes include the title prefix, shortened explanations and headings, additional experimental discussion, and new Acknowledgments and Impact Statement sections. The conclusion is relabeled to explicitly mention limitations.
descriptions.P2: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, extensively repositions and resizes displays, and condenses Tables 1-3. It adds ablation, domain-gap, and trajectory displays while removing v1's bike, car, and painting galleries (Figures 12, 13, and 17). These are presentation changes beyond renumbering.

P-037A3AEEDF.title: Merging Triggers, Breaking Backdoors: Defensive Poisoning for Instruction-Tuned Language Models

descriptions.M1: The defensive-poisoning procedure, default trigger–response construction, and training objective in Equations 1–3 remain unchanged. Weight Recovery is renamed Backdoor Neutralization; PCA measurements and semantic-response variants are introduced as analyses of the existing method.
descriptions.E1: The existing datasets and Toxic/Refusal tasks are retained. Appendix G adds a limited input scenario: Llama2-7B is attacked using the natural prompt prefix 'As my personal assistant,' extending trigger coverage without adding a dataset or application domain.
descriptions.E2: The corresponding comparisons in Table 1 and v1 Table 3/v2 Table 5 retain Clean-FFT, ONION, Fine-mixing, and the clean/attacked reference models. No comparison method is added, removed, or substantively redefined.
descriptions.E3: V2 extends evaluation procedures with final-hidden-state PCA overlap, BLEU-2/ROUGE comparisons, attack-poisoning ratios of 10–30%, defensive-poisoning ratios of 0.001–0.01, and lambda values of 0.01–1.0. The original model lineup, splits, budgets, and main evaluation protocol remain unchanged. The 20% attack default was already stated in v1.
descriptions.E4: Beyond the retained trigger-count, behavioral-mixing, and poisoned-head analyses, v2 adds representation and lexical-overlap analyses, three hyperparameter sensitivity studies, coherent-versus-random defensive-response ablations, and a semantic-trigger robustness test (Section 5.2 and Appendices E–G). These examine previously untested mechanisms, design choices, and failure conditions.
descriptions.E5: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The new average overlap scores are additional results, without an accompanying change in uncertainty-reporting practices.
descriptions.E6: The matched original tables retain their numerical values. V2 adds findings in Tables 2–3 and 6–10, including mean subspace overlaps of 0.558 for Toxic and 0.619 for Refusal, failures with coherent defensive responses, and defended semantic-trigger ASRs of 0.000 and 0.014. These are newly reported analyses and scenarios, rather than improvements to the original benchmark scores.
descriptions.T1: Section 5.2 introduces formal definitions of attacker- and defender-induced hidden-state shifts and a PCA projection-overlap ratio in Equations 4–6. The method equations and existing attention-head criterion are retained; no theorem or proof is added.
descriptions.C1: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of a two-stage, trigger-agnostic, data-efficient defense that reduces attack success while preserving instruction-following ability. The additional experiments support these existing contributions without materially redefining their scope.
descriptions.C2: V2 interprets the new measurements as partial representation sharing with preserved output diversity. Appendix F adds an explanation that coherent defensive responses overlap with clean-response features, so suppressing them can damage utility; Appendix E explains poisoning-rate and loss-weight tradeoffs. The pretraining-scale explanation is also softened to a plausible explanation.
descriptions.D1: Section 4.3 newly specifies the default lambda as 0.1, and Appendix A fills v1's missing gradient-accumulation value with 8. New appendices document tested parameter ranges and coherent response templates. These are disclosures rather than established changes to the original training runs; hardware, optimizer, learning rates, and training times are retained.
descriptions.R1: The reference lists match after normalizing line wrapping. Related-work coverage and the positioning against existing classification and generative backdoor defenses remain substantively unchanged.
descriptions.P1: V2 standardizes stage names, corrects local grammar and model-label errors, and updates headings and cross-references. Section 5.2 and Appendices E–G are inserted, with subsequent material renumbered; the existing narrative is largely retained.
descriptions.P2: Seven new tables—Tables 2–3 and 6–10—expand the displayed evidence, sometimes reusing original default results as reference rows. Original Tables 2–3 become Tables 4–5. The pipeline labels and SCPN/Syntactic heatmap label are updated, and figures and appendix material are repositioned.

P-4F3A1AD868.title: Refracting Reality: Generating Images with Realistic Transparent Objects

descriptions.M1: Object placement changes from a geometry-based horizontal-surface heuristic with a 1.5 m floor-exclusion threshold in v1 Appendix C to SAM 3 segmentation of the prompt-specified surface in v2 Appendix B. The core ray tracing, cross-view synchronization, Fresnel blending and denoising procedures remain unchanged.
descriptions.E1: Coverage expands from six indoor scene prompts to ten indoor/outdoor categories, adding cave, desert, karaoke and landscape scenes. V2 also evaluates captured indoor and outdoor photographs. The six object geometries are not newly introduced: v1 already includes the non-spherical objects in its appendix.
descriptions.E2: V2 retains FLUX inpainting and the original FLUX generation comparator, now labeled FLUX-dev, and adds FLUX.2-dev, Qwen-Image and Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large. Their participation is demonstrated in Tables 1 and 3 and Figure 9, broadening comparison beyond the original two FLUX baselines.
descriptions.E3: V2 introduces an explicit design crossing five variations per prompt with six geometries, averaging results over 300 scene-object combinations. It also adds qualitative testing using fixed-camera photographs captured with and without a sphere. The existing metrics, 20 denoising steps, guidance scale and image resolutions remain unchanged.
descriptions.E4: V2 Table 2 and Figure 6 directly test reflection modeling and panorama synchronization, and Table 2 explicitly compares relighting effects. These extend analysis of the central mechanisms. The original DPA, LPW and time-travel ablations are retained as Figure 13 and Table 4; refractive-index and time-travel sensitivity analyses also remain.
descriptions.E5: Both versions retain the same seed-matching statement and report point estimates without confidence intervals, dispersion estimates or significance tests. V2's prompt variations and newly disclosed repeated relighting concern evaluation coverage and output selection, not statistical uncertainty estimation.
descriptions.E6: The main aggregate comparison is replaced and expanded: Snellcaster's PSNR/LPIPS are 17.10/0.28 in v1 Table 1 and 16.51/0.24 in v2 Table 1 under different benchmark coverage, so these are not matched-setting performance changes. V2 adds baseline scores, mechanism-ablation results and captured-scene outputs. Its expanded comparison shows leading refraction metrics, but not leading CLIP or ImageReward.
descriptions.T1: Equations 1-14, including flow matching, ray paths, Snell's law, synchronization and Fresnel blending, are unchanged. The single-object and uniform-refractive-index assumptions remain, with no added or revised theorem, proof or derivation.
descriptions.C1: The abstract, introduction's three contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: training-free transparent-object generation using physical refraction constraints and synchronized perspective/panoramic views. The expanded experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine them.
descriptions.C2: V2 Section 5.3 adds explanations for panorama synchronization's greater measured contribution relative to reflections and explicitly discusses relighting's trade-off between pixel accuracy and visual plausibility. Existing qualifications about Blender references, time-travel smoothing and future extensions largely remain unchanged.
descriptions.D1: V2 newly documents repeating relighting 20 times and selecting by object-region PSNR, provides additional scene prompts, specifies the retained ablation's six-scene sphere scope, and clarifies that the unchanged 126-second runtime excludes preprocessing. V1 does not establish whether the relighting selection procedure was already used.
descriptions.R1: Four references are added for SAM 3 and the additional FLUX.2, Qwen-Image and Stable Diffusion comparisons. Section 2's related-work discussion and the positioning relative to synchronization and light-transport research remain substantively unchanged.
descriptions.P1: Experimental descriptions and the main ablation discussion are revised, prompt documentation is merged with object-parameter extraction, and the original ablation discussion moves to the appendix. References move before the supplement. Most introductory, methodological and concluding prose remains intact.
descriptions.P2: The empirical presentation is redesigned: Figures 1 and 3 change examples, new Figures 5-6 show captured scenes and central-component ablations, and Figure 9 becomes a broader comparison grid. Table 1 changes to an all-method summary, the expanded per-scene table is split into two panels, and the original ablation figure moves to the appendix.

P-AFC3BFEAA7.title: GrOCE : Graph-Guided Online Concept Erasure for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

descriptions.M1: v1 Sections 3.3–3.4 diffuse over the global graph and subtract weighted semantic projections from token embeddings. v2 Sections 4.2–4.3 restrict diffusion to an n-hop subgraph and replace embedding subtraction with influence-threshold token removal followed by prompt re-encoding. These change the inference procedure substantially.
descriptions.E1: Beyond the retained character and artistic-style evaluations, v2 adds quantitative violence, shooting, and pornography erasure and qualitative emotion, action, and abstract-category scenarios (Table S1; Figures S6 and S8–S11). v2 also omits v1's statement about 25 celebrity templates, although neither PDF presents identifiable celebrity results.
descriptions.E2: Corresponding comparisons retain ConAbl, MACE, SPEED, and AdaVD. SD v1.4 was already reported in v1's tables despite only being added to the baseline paragraph in v2. Table S1 extends the existing comparator set to sensitive concepts.
descriptions.E3: The retained benchmark protocol still uses DPM-solver, 30 sampling steps, guidance 7.5, and ten images per template and concept. Added experiments introduce a with/without-Identify control and SD 1.5, SD 2.1, and SD 3.0 configurations. The sensitivity evaluation changes from relational ratio, runtime, and graph degree to CS/FID over K, gamma, and delta.
descriptions.E4: v2 adds the Identify-removal ablation (Table 3), additional backbone demonstrations, and abstract-neighbor erasure case studies. v1's n/K/tau study in Figure 4 is replaced, rather than relocated, by a different K/gamma/delta study in Figure S12; the original radius and graph-sparsification analyses disappear.
descriptions.E5: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence levels, or significance tests. Both hyperparameter figures contain shaded bands without defining their statistical meaning; v2 establishes no changed uncertainty-reporting procedure.
descriptions.E6: In Table 1's triple-erasure setting, Pikachu FID changes from 24.51 to 43.86 for ConAbl, 18.15 to 92.74 for MACE, and 20.37 to 25.67 for SPEED. GrOCE's main-table scores remain unchanged. v2 adds results, including ablation CS/FID of 14.51/426.74 without Identify versus 16.92/0 with it, sensitive-concept scores in Table S1, and supplementary qualitative and sensitivity findings.
descriptions.T1: The mathematical operators change substantively: global-graph heat diffusion and normalized weighted embedding subtraction in v1 Equations 4–7 become subgraph diffusion and an L2-threshold token-retention rule in v2 Equations 5–9. These are non-equivalent definitions, beyond notation changes. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.
descriptions.C1: v2 removes the introduction's explicit claim of theoretical guarantees and recasts the conclusion's complete semantic removal through spectral diffusion as precise, context-aware suppression. The central claims of training-free online erasure and state-of-the-art accuracy, preservation, and efficiency remain.
descriptions.C2: v2 adds explanations that local diffusion reduces distant-node noise and that Identify prevents collateral erasure, supported by the new ablation. The supplement interprets additional examples as evidence of broader applicability and cluster-wide suppression, and replaces the earlier hyperparameter discussion with K/gamma/delta tradeoffs. Most main-result interpretations remain unchanged.
descriptions.D1: v2 specifies previously unreported or newly relevant settings: lambda=0.1, phi=3, gamma=0.8, and delta=10. Its code link changes from an anonymous repository to MagicCat-AI/GrOCE on GitHub. The explicit PyTorch and all-experiments-on-A100 disclosure disappears, although A100 hardware remains specified for timing.
descriptions.R1: v2 adds citations including CURE, Selective Amnesia, Receler, and Detect-and-Guide, while removing works including ACE, GLIDE, and BUSTER. The central positioning against locally acting erasure methods remains. Publication updates for retained works such as SPEED and TRCE are bibliographic changes.
descriptions.P1: The abstract, introduction passages, method exposition, and conclusion are rewritten. Preliminaries become a separate section, related work is consolidated from three categories into two, and component terminology is standardized as Construct, Identify, and Sever. This is extensive editorial restructuring beyond the added experiments.
descriptions.P2: Figure 2 is redrawn to depict prompt-token removal, and Tables 1–2 receive revised rules and highlighting. Existing style and backbone figures move. v2 adds the component-ablation table, Table S1, eleven supplementary image grids, and the replacement sensitivity display in Figure S12.

P-ED7ABD4AB8.title: SOCO: Benchmarking Semantic Object Correspondence in Vision Foundation Models

descriptions.M1: The SOC framework, feature matching in Equation 1, frozen-backbone probes and LVLM evaluation procedure are unchanged.
descriptions.E1: Both versions evaluate the same SOCO categories and tasks, other correspondence benchmarks in Appendix C.1, and downstream tasks in Section 5.3. Added citations in Table 1 do not expand evaluated coverage.
descriptions.E2: The evaluated model and comparator sets in the main and appendix experiments are unchanged. DiscoBox already appeared in Table 1; its new citation does not introduce an evaluated baseline.
descriptions.E3: Both retain the same sampling, metrics, resolutions and probe settings, including 20,000 pairs per CC/SOC/Cross-SOC task and the four-permutation CircularEval protocol for LVLMs.
descriptions.E4: Appendix A retains the same threshold, viewpoint, category and alternative evaluation-protocol analyses. Appendix D.4 retains the same visual-marker shape and color tests.
descriptions.E5: Section 5.3 retains 95% bootstrap confidence intervals using 10,000 resamples and leave-one-out checks. Run, seed and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged throughout.
descriptions.E6: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main paper and appendices. For example, DINOv2 SOC PCK remains 60.4 in Table 2, and Qwen3-VL-8B description-only accuracy remains 54.0 in Table 3.
descriptions.T1: The definitions of semantic concepts, SOC and cross-category correspondence in Section 3.2, along with the mathematical evaluation formulations, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.
descriptions.C1: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions and claims about geometric part awareness, the LVLM text-versus-visual correspondence gap, and SOC's downstream diagnostic value.
descriptions.C2: Interpretations of repeated-part confusion, cross-category transfer and LVLM behavior are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same limitations concerning sparse annotations, image-source bias, prompting, nearest-neighbor matching and taxonomy scope.
descriptions.D1: Appendices D–E retain the same model configurations, implementation details, prompts and annotation procedures. The project link and dataset/evaluation-framework release statements are unchanged.
descriptions.R1: v4 adds the DiscoBox paper by Lan et al. as reference 33 and cites it in the existing Table 1 row. Table 1 also gains citations to already-referenced datasets. The related-work argument and novelty positioning remain unchanged.
descriptions.P1: Bibliographic edits revise author information, add publication page ranges and expand venue names. Citation numbering and the arXiv version/date change, while the scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.
descriptions.P2: Figure 1 has small visual adjustments while retaining its content. Table 1 widens slightly to accommodate citations, and the bibliography reflows. Experimental figures and tables retain their designs.

P-FDA830A64E.title: OneTwoVLA: A Unified Vision-Language-Action Model with Adaptive Reasoning

descriptions.M1: V1 describes manually annotated robot reasoning. V2 introduces a two-stage Gemini annotation pipeline using sampled demonstration frames, interval identification and reasoning-content assembly, with recovery and dialogue extensions in Appendix D. This adds a data-curation component. The controller architecture, losses and adaptive inference algorithm remain unchanged.
descriptions.E1: V2 adds testing on 20 novel human-robot interaction scenarios in Hotpot and Cocktail and describes interaction content in synthetic planning data. The three long-horizon tasks, four generalizable-planning tasks, grounding environments and robot platforms already appear in v1, including its appendices.
descriptions.E2: V2 Figure 6 adds π0 and robot-only OneTwoVLA comparisons on the existing generalizable-planning tasks; Figure 2 includes Dual-System in task-time comparisons. The original long-horizon and grounding comparator sets remain unchanged. Changing the dual-system baseline's cited inspiration from ViLa to Hi Robot does not establish a different Gemini-plus-π0 implementation.
descriptions.E3: V2 adds quantitative evaluation designs for generalizable planning, recovery conditional on errors, subtask-level interaction, novel interaction scenarios and annotation quality, including a 50-instance synthetic-data audit. Existing training budgets and grounding protocols are retained. Newly specifying the placement range and recovery-demonstration subsets does not establish that those settings changed.
descriptions.E4: V2 adds a with/without-VL comparison for generalizable planning, examines interaction generalization, evaluates automatic robot-annotation quality and audits synthetic-image/text errors. These extend the analysis of co-training and data quality beyond v1's examples. Existing multimodality, reasoning-action consistency and failure-case analyses are retained.
descriptions.E5: Neither version reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional episode counts and audit frequencies in v2 provide sample sizes and results without introducing uncertainty reporting.
descriptions.E6: The original long-horizon and grounding scores are retained. V2 newly reports generalizable-planning averages of 70% for OneTwoVLA-VL, 10% for OneTwoVLA and 6% for π0; quantitative recovery and interaction comparisons; 72.5% novel-interaction success; task timings; and annotation-quality findings, including 40 fully correct synthetic samples out of 50. These are added results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under matched settings.
descriptions.T1: V2 Section 3.2 and Appendix D add formal specifications of ordered plans, reasoning intervals, history/next-step construction and dialogue-conditioned plan updates for automated annotation. The original policy formulation and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged, and no theorems or proofs are added.
descriptions.C1: The abstract, introductory contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims: unified adaptive reasoning and acting, synthetic vision-language co-training, and four demonstrated robot capabilities. The added methods and evidence do not redefine these headline contributions.
descriptions.C2: V2 reframes the annotation limitation around hand-selected reasoning-step heuristics and adds a potential action-inference bottleneck when scaling model size. It also interprets the new planning controls as showing limited generalization without VL co-training. Existing mechanism explanations and appendix failure cases remain.
descriptions.D1: V2 supplies annotation instructions: 32-frame sampling, midpoint selection, content assembly, recovery/dialogue handling and complete prompt templates with output schemas and visibility/gripper constraints. It also discloses baseline invocation scheduling, placement randomization and recovery-data subsets. The existing training hardware, budgets and deployment details are retained.
descriptions.R1: V2 adds ECoT-Lite and discusses its reasoning-efficiency and interaction tradeoffs, changes the baseline's cited inspiration to Hi Robot, and removes several background references concerning recovery, interaction and reinforcement learning. The broad positioning against separated reasoning/action systems remains unchanged.
descriptions.P1: Most prose and the main narrative sequence are retained, with localized method and experiment expansions. Co-training related work moves to Appendix B, conclusion and limitations are combined, and an LLM-usage statement is added. Author affiliations, acknowledgments, headings and citation style are also revised.
descriptions.P2: V1's long-horizon results table becomes a bar chart paired with new generalization results. V2 adds a timing chart, recovery and interaction tables, a quality-audit table and two annotation-prompt figures. It also adopts the ICLR layout and redistributes several appendix tables, environment illustrations and prompts across pages.

descriptions.M1: The objective, gradient-weighted covariance, eigenvector selection, keeping-ratio rule, and compressed weight and bias construction remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. Expanded derivations and implementation disclosures do not introduce a new procedure.
descriptions.E1: Both versions evaluate mathematical reasoning on GSM8K/MATH and code generation on HumanEval/MBPP. v4 names MetaMathQA-395K and Code-Instructions-120K as calibration sources for these existing experiments; it does not establish that calibration coverage was added or replaced.
descriptions.E2: ASVD moves from citation-only coverage in v2 to evaluated comparisons across all four benchmarks in v4 Figures 2–5 and Tables 6–9. Quantization comparisons also add 8-bit AFM in Tables 1–2. These expand the relevant controls. ASVD is mentioned in Section 4.5 but is absent from the corresponding inference Figure 8 and Table 14.
descriptions.E3: New experiments introduce an η sweep over 0, 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75 at keeping ratios of 50%, 60%, and 70%, and a single-A100 profiling-cost comparison. Existing evaluation tasks, model families, Pass@1 metric, and pre/post-compression finetuning sequence remain. Newly specified optimizer and calibration settings do not establish changes to earlier protocols.
descriptions.E4: v4 adds four-layer importance-matrix heatmaps and distributions in Appendix B.1, plus the η sensitivity study in B.2; neither analysis appears in v2. B.3 additionally reports calibration-size convergence qualitatively, without a detailed sweep. These extend the mechanism and sensitivity evidence beyond the retained gradient-magnitude illustration.
descriptions.E5: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty across repeated evaluations. The new importance-matrix histograms and quantiles describe matrix entries rather than experimental uncertainty.
descriptions.E6: Many IMPACT/AFM size–accuracy entries are replaced, alongside new comparator and analysis results. Uncompressed CodeLlama HumanEval scores change from 36.0% to 45.1% for 7B and 45.7% to 52.4% for 13B (v2 Tables 6–7; v4 Tables 8–9). Maximum reported Llama 2-7B GSM8K size reduction changes from 48.6% to 55.4%, while CodeLlama-7B HumanEval reduction changes from 48.9% to 24.2%. These are revised reports, not established same-setting gains; compression points and comparator membership also change.
descriptions.T1: Appendix A.1 corrects the QM–AM equality condition. A.2 revises the bounding argument through absolute component products and QM–AM before approximately factorizing the expectation of squared terms, replacing v2's earlier mean-product step. The theorem statements and closed-form solution remain unchanged.
descriptions.C1: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion strengthen the quantitative compression claim from up to 48.6% to 55.4% greater size reduction. The principal novelty claim and contribution of performance-aware activation reconstruction through a weighted-covariance eigensolution remain unchanged.
descriptions.C2: Appendix B newly interprets long-tailed importance values as emphasizing rare critical interactions, explains profiling overhead through backward passes and ASVD rank search, and explicitly states calibration-distribution dependence alongside architecture-generic applicability. These add substantive explanations and qualifications to the retained interpretation.
descriptions.D1: V2 gives little experimental implementation information. V4 Section 4.1 and Appendix B.3 disclose calibration datasets and fractions, AdamW learning rates, cosine scheduling, warmup, BF16, FSDP, batch sizes, GPU allocation, and profiling hardware/cost. These disclosures do not establish that the previously used settings changed.
descriptions.R1: v4 adds calibration-data references, sensitivity-based pruning references supporting Taylor approximations, and brief discussion of trustworthiness, structured pruning, and token compression. It also identifies Li et al. (2025a) as the source of several baseline results. The central positioning and claimed novelty remain intact.
descriptions.P1: The abstract is rewritten, local explanations and cross-references are refined, and Appendix B gains four named subsections. Affiliations, publication information, Limitations, and Acknowledgments are added. The main section sequence and much of the existing prose remain.
descriptions.P2: v4 adds Figures 9–10 and ablation, profiling-cost, and throughput tables; redraws comparison plots with expanded legends and changed HumanEval axes; and moves the 13B quantization figure into the main text. v2 Tables 4–7 are split into performance Tables 6–9 and reduction Tables 10–13. Page format, typography, and table placement also change substantially.

P-ECDC66BB4C.title: What is the Right Embedding Space for Contrastive Learning in Referring Expression Counting?

descriptions.M1: V1 selects positive tokens by cosine similarity to the class-masked referring expression, taking the top N tokens. V2 instead uses bipartite matching between predicted locations and ground-truth points, changing the contrastive labeling procedure and supervision. It also integrates C-REX into GroundingREC and CAD-GD by replacing their image-text losses while retaining their other objectives. The positive-anchor contrastive loss itself remains unchanged.
descriptions.E1: REC-8K and FSC-147 remain, but v2 removes the CARPK drone/parking-lot evaluation, eliminating v1's separate cross-dataset transfer test. V2 adds evaluation on paraphrased REC-8K expressions, introducing a linguistic-variation scenario.
descriptions.E2: V2 adds CAD-GD comparisons, including its density-guided inference variant, and Molmo2-4B. The FSC-147 comparison removes exemplar-based methods including FamNet, BMNet+, CounTR, and CACViT. Earlier REC comparators such as ZSC, TFOC, CounTX, and CountGD remain in supplementary Tables 6–7; their relocation is not removal.
descriptions.E3: Reported detection thresholds change from 0.30/0.36 to 0.25/0.35 for CLS/other tokens. V2 adds Swin-B configurations alongside Swin-T, reports precision and recall separately, evaluates density-guided CAD-GD inference, and specifies zero-shot and two-shot Molmo protocols. The count-range analysis also merges the three lowest bins into 0–20. These are substantive protocol changes, beyond newly disclosed training details.
descriptions.E4: V2 adds image-text versus image-only versus joint-loss ablations and paraphrase robustness testing. Its selection ablation adds bipartite matching and removes the N + 2log2(N) alternative. Count-range and qualitative analyses expand to paired comparisons across three architectures, while v1's attribute-wise MAE analysis and centroid-baseline component ablation disappear. The positive-anchor loss ablation is retained in Table 4b.
descriptions.E5: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The sample counts accompanying count-range plots describe evaluation examples, not repeated runs.
descriptions.E6: V1's REC MAE/RMSE of 5.06/17.53 survives as the top-N ablation in v2 Table 4a. New matching-based GroundingDINO+C-REX results are 4.38/17.93 with Swin-T and 4.20/16.76 with Swin-B. V2 adds extensive architecture, paraphrase, and Molmo results while removing CARPK and attribute-level scores. Findings include CAD-GD paraphrase MAE worsening from 6.85 to 8.02 with C-REX. Changed methods and protocols preclude treating cross-version scores as same-setting gains.
descriptions.T1: The positive-set definition changes from the cosine-similarity arg-top-N construction in v1 Equations 2–3 to location-based bipartite matching in v2 Section 3. The supervised and modified contrastive-loss formulas otherwise remain algebraically unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.
descriptions.C1: V1 presents identifying centroid prediction as a key counting component and constructing an improved baseline as central contributions. V2 drops that emphasis and foregrounds C-REX as a plug-in applicable to any REC architecture, demonstrated on three architectures. Its headline improvement claims change from over 22% MAE and 10% RMSE to up to 28% and 24.5% under the revised comparisons.
descriptions.C2: V2 introduces discussion of negative-token scarcity in extremely dense scenes and potential scaling with larger backbones. It interprets the joint-loss and Molmo experiments as support for specialized visual supervision, explicitly qualifies paraphrase robustness for CAD-GD, and illustrates accurate-looking counts that still select incorrect instances in Figure 8. V1's top-N label-noise justification and centroid-centered explanations are removed.
descriptions.D1: V2 newly documents 20/30-epoch training schedules, learning-rate decay, checkpoint/retraining provenance, and CAD-GD density-map construction. It omits v1's explicit AdamW optimizer, weight decay of 1e-4, and loss weights of 1, 5, and 0.005. The direct code-repository link becomes a project-page link. These are documentation and access-instruction changes; the PDFs do not establish changes to omitted parameters or actual resource availability.
descriptions.R1: V2 expands research positioning: CAD-GD becomes an important REC predecessor, counting VQA is distinguished from localized REC, intra-image contrastive learning is related to person re-identification, and VLM/tool-based counting is discussed. These additions introduce substantive comparisons and citations beyond v1's focus on GroundingREC and detection-versus-density counting.
descriptions.P1: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around embedding-space choice and architectural portability. The baseline-centered method subsection disappears, remaining method explanations are reordered and expanded, and the supplementary narrative is reorganized. This is editorial restructuring beyond adding experiments.
descriptions.P2: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. The original pipeline figure is replaced by two conceptual comparisons, tables are rebuilt around paired baseline/C-REX configurations and backbones, and qualitative grids are extensively revised. The earlier REC comparison is split and moved to supplementary tables; the count-range plot is regrouped and the attribute-wise chart removed.

P-681117A4BE.title: Adaptive Physics Transformer with Fused Global-Local Attention for Subsurface Energy Systems

descriptions.M1: The fused global/local encoder, gating, latent approximator, decoder, temporal conditioning and training objective remain unchanged in Section 2 and Appendix B. The new scaling experiments vary model width without introducing a new APT component or procedure.
descriptions.E1: New Appendix D adds Airfoil, Darcy and Elasticity evaluations, covering compressible flow, linear porous-medium flow and linear solid mechanics. This extends task coverage beyond the retained subsurface and CarBench experiments. The scaling studies reuse ATES.
descriptions.E2: Table 1 adds Transolver, MINO, UPT and HOOD to the faulted CO2 comparison. Table 3 adds evaluated UPT and Transolver baselines on ATES and records an attempted MINO evaluation that exceeds memory capacity. These additions broaden comparisons on existing tasks; the earlier comparators remain.
descriptions.E3: Section 4.5 introduces controlled experiments with 40k, 120k and 161k training samples and 0.8M, 17.5M and 69.4M parameters, reporting the best test loss during training. New baseline experiments specify additional training budgets and configurations. The faulted-CO2 timing protocol changes its reported GPU from A100 to H100, except HOOD on A100, and newly specifies batch size 340; these are not directly comparable timing conditions across versions.
descriptions.E4: Section 4.5 and Table 7 add data-size and model-capacity sensitivity studies, testing whether additional data and parameters continue improving ATES predictions. Section 4.3 also expands analysis of accuracy, latency and memory tradeoffs. Existing branch ablations, super-resolution tests, geological distribution-shift tests and qualitative cases are retained.
descriptions.E5: No changed run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimators, confidence intervals or significance procedures are documented. The existing uncertainty descriptions and CarBench sampling-seed caveat remain. Changes to CarBench uncertainty values are numerical result changes, without evidence of a changed estimation procedure.
descriptions.E6: v2 adds baseline, scaling, efficiency and PDE results while retaining the main APT accuracy scores. Table 7 reports losses falling from 0.1153 to 0.0812 with increased data and from 0.1167 to 0.0722 with increased model size. CarBench changes from 96.00±3.1 to 96.00±0.18 for R2 and from 0.1535±0.038 to 0.1535±0.0022 for relative L2. The timing table replaces APT's 0.017 s with 0.002 s under different hardware. New Table 17 places APT second on Airfoil and Elasticity but third on Darcy, contrary to its caption.
descriptions.T1: The operator formulation, loss, conditioning equations, metric definitions and governing-PDE assumptions in Section 2 and Appendices B–C are retained. The new mesh-adaptivity taxonomy is descriptive and introduces no new formal result, proof or derivation.
descriptions.C1: The abstract adds an explicit claim of favorable scaling behavior and narrows the first-architecture claim from adaptive mesh refinement generally to HR-adaptive simulations. The central claims about fused attention, mesh flexibility, super-resolution and cross-dataset learning remain.
descriptions.C2: v2 interprets the new scaling results as showing further growth potential and explains MINO's ATES memory failure through its mesh-dependent latent size. Appendix D emphasizes that APT's advantage is strongest in heterogeneous subsurface settings. The conclusion newly acknowledges that scaling was demonstrated for one physics type and leaves multiphysics pretraining and transfer fine-tuning untested.
descriptions.D1: Appendices C.1.2 and C.2.1 expand implementation documentation for the added baselines, including widths, layers, tokens, graph hierarchy, optimizer settings and training budgets. v2 also specifies timing batch size and hardware and documents scaling configurations. Existing APT implementation descriptions and the promise to release code and created datasets upon publication remain.
descriptions.R1: v2 adds HOOD and MINO citations and introduces Appendix A.5 distinguishing R-, H- and HR-adaptivity. It explicitly credits UPT's earlier ability to query different input/output mesh topologies, refining APT's novelty positioning. Other reference changes largely update bibliographic metadata or remove duplicate entries.
descriptions.P1: v2 adds focused efficiency and scaling subsections, a mesh-adaptivity subsection, Appendix D and a limitations paragraph. Existing prose and section organization are largely retained, with localized grammar, reference and conference-header edits.
descriptions.P2: v2 adds the accuracy–latency–memory plot in Figure 4 and new scaling and PDE tables, while expanding the baseline and timing tables with rows, groups and footnotes. Existing figures and most table designs are retained, with localized relocation, renumbering and page reflow.

P-2291B7799A.title: Multi-Scale Local Speculative Decoding for Image Generation

descriptions.M1: v2 adds whole-image drafting with ZipAR and parallel resampling across rejection islands, with ZipAR also operating within islands (Section 3.4). It additionally introduces a training-free pixel-space upsampling route and makes it the default. v1 used learned latent up/down-samplers with sequential drafting and resampling.
descriptions.E1: Both versions retain LAION-COCO-Aesthetic training data, GenEval and DPG-Bench evaluation, and MS-COCO 2017 validation images for perceptual metrics. Text-to-image generation at 512p and 1024p remains the task coverage. Adding Tar-7B and LlamaGen changes model configurations rather than datasets or tasks.
descriptions.E2: v2 removes Table 1's entire broad cross-model comparison block, including Chameleon, Lumina-mGPT, Transfusion, Show-O, Janus/Janus-Pro, D-DiT, Emu3, and Harmon. The comparison consequently focuses on acceleration within base generators. ZipAR-16, EAGLE-2, and LANTERN remain the principal acceleration comparators and are also evaluated on the added model configurations.
descriptions.E3: Evaluation expands from Tar-1.5B alone to Tar-7B at both resolutions and LlamaGen-XL at 512p. v2 also introduces parallel-versus-sequential evaluations at matched acceptance thresholds. The existing metrics, A100/batch-one timing setup, and supplementary 500-prompt latency protocol remain; the retained latency description still excludes MLLM conditioning time.
descriptions.E4: Figure 5d adds an ablation testing parallel decoding, and Figure 7 adds component-level latency breakdowns with parallel decoding enabled. Figure 5a removes the DINO-discriminator variant and adds the pixel-space upsampler comparison. Probability-pooling, local-expansion, and supplementary neighborhood-radius ablations are retained.
descriptions.E5: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands. The revised tables and plots retain point-estimate reporting.
descriptions.E6: Table 1 replaces MuLo-SD results with results for the revised default: Tar-1.5B/1024p changes from 1.68x speedup and 76.3 GenEval to 3.90x and 76.8. New Tar-7B/1024p results report 5.33x and 85.4. New LlamaGen results report 1.40x, below LANTERN's 1.59x and ZipAR's 1.88x. These involve changed method configurations; supplementary curves and qualitative outputs are also revised.
descriptions.T1: v2 Equation 8 newly defines rejection islands as disjoint 8-connected components partitioning the expanded rejection set. Existing acceptance rules, neighborhood definitions, and the theoretical sequential-speedup expression remain mathematically equivalent. No new theorem or proof is supplied.
descriptions.C1: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion elevate parallel-decoding integration from proposed future work to a third central contribution. The headline speedup changes from approximately 1.7x to 5x, and claimed superiority expands from speculative-decoding baselines to parallel decoding, including ZipAR.
descriptions.C2: New Section 4.5 identifies memory costs from two checkpoints/KV caches and dependence on drafter-verifier distributional alignment, linking weaker LlamaGen gains to this limitation and proposing self-speculation as a remedy. v2 also explains choosing the training-free pixel upsampler despite weaker isolated performance, whereas v1 selected the learned PatchGAN variant for its trade-off.
descriptions.D1: v2 identifies HIT-SR as the pixel-space super-resolution component. It removes explicit Tar, ZipAR, and LANTERN repository links and v1's training-time/hardware disclosure and hinge-loss, LeCam, and augmentation details. Most learned-sampler architecture, optimizer, batch-size, training-step, and inference-hyperparameter information remains in the supplement; these omissions do not establish changed training procedures.
descriptions.R1: v2 adds references for connected-component labeling and HIT-SR, while removing works supporting deleted comparisons or training discussion, including ImageFolder and Projected GANs. ZipAR is repositioned as an implemented component rather than only a prospective combination. The broader positioning relative to LANTERN and multi-scale autoregressive models remains substantially intact.
descriptions.P1: v2 condenses the preliminaries and multi-scale motivation, separates implementation details from experimental settings, and introduces parallel-decoding and limitations subsections. Much wording and the overall introduction–related work–method–experiments–conclusion–supplement structure remain recognizable.
descriptions.P2: Table 1 is reorganized around generator/resolution configurations. Figure 3 is redrawn to show rejection islands, Figure 4 expands from six to eight examples, Figure 5 gains a fourth panel, and Figure 7 becomes a sequential/parallel four-panel comparison. Figure 8 changes axis ranges, qualitative displays are refreshed, and document typography changes throughout.

P-52F54860D9.title: Training-free Mixed-Resolution Latent Upsampling for Spatially Accelerated Diffusion Transformers

descriptions.M1: The core procedure remains low-resolution denoising, selective early upsampling using decoded Canny edges, and full-resolution refinement, with correlated noise and JSD-based timestep matching. NT-DM becomes NT-Matching, but its underlying algorithm remains equivalent. Additional positional-embedding explanations and experiments with other acceleration methods do not establish a changed RALU algorithm.
descriptions.E1: Appendix B.4 changes T2I-CompBench coverage from complex/texture to spatial/non-spatial/complex and narrows GenEval from six categories to four. CC12M remains. v3 newly identifies MS-COCO for image-quality evaluation, but v2 leaves that data source unspecified, so this alone does not establish an added dataset.
descriptions.E2: v3 Table 1 adds evaluated FLUX comparisons with Delta-DiT, TeaCache, and TaylorSeer, and SD3 comparisons with Delta-DiT, ToCa, and TaylorSeer. v2 principally compared against ToCa or RAS and Bottleneck Sampling. The integration comparison also replaces the earlier custom caching configuration with named temporal acceleration methods.
descriptions.E3: FID is replaced by ImageReward, and new artifact-rate and edge-energy evaluations are introduced. The FLUX 4× configuration with 18 RALU steps is replaced by a 5× configuration with 15 steps. New protocols include 100-image artifact analyses, four-step distilled-model integrations, and A6000 benchmarking. The retained FLUX 7× and SD3 stage counts merely change from per-stage to cumulative notation.
descriptions.E4: v3 extends v2's qualitative upsampling-timing study and limited parameter ablations with systematic timing/JSD analyses, artifact rate versus FLOPs, and quantitative ratio sweeps. Appendix C adds image-space versus latent-space edge detection, fixed versus adaptive selection, interpolation comparisons, and edge-mask visualizations. These directly test previously unsupported design choices.
descriptions.E5: v3 adds error bars in Figures 2–3, a p < 0.001 statement for the ImageReward/JSD relationship, and FLOP mean±standard deviation in Table S4. GenEval reporting changes from fixed-seed wording to four different seeds per prompt. The error-bar definition and significance-test procedure remain unspecified; the wording does not establish increased repeated runs.
descriptions.E6: v3 adds or replaces extensive results, including ImageReward scores, expanded comparisons, distilled-model integrations, hardware measurements, and artifact ablations. For retained FLUX 7× RALU, reported latency changes from 3.37 to 3.75 seconds, while NIQE 6.87 and CLIP-IQA 0.681 remain unchanged. T2I-CompBench/GenEval change from 0.566/0.646 to 0.633/0.682 under revised task coverage, so these are not established same-setting gains.
descriptions.T1: v3 Eqs. (5)–(6) correct the main-text matching target to a latent with isotropic covariance, replacing v2 Eq. (5)'s upsampled-latent target. Appendix A.1 adds consequences for intermediate and fully denoised endpoints. The rescheduling formulas otherwise remain equivalent, and the appendix's inconsistent covariance expressions in Eqs. (S2) and (S4) persist.
descriptions.C1: The claims of training-free spatial acceleration up to 7× on FLUX and 3× on SD3 remain. However, v3 adds compatibility with timestep-distilled models and elevates combined acceleration up to 15.9× to an abstract claim and principal contribution. Table 2 identifies these speedups as FLOP-based, extending applicability beyond the earlier caching-integration claim.
descriptions.C2: v3 adds rationales for image-space Canny detection, fixed selection ratios, and nearest-neighbor interpolation. Section 6 introduces a tentative token-merging analogy while acknowledging that mixed-resolution self-attention remains unexplained. Appendix D emphasizes untested U-Net backbones instead of v2's explicit audio/3D examples, while retaining the limitation to flow-matching models.
descriptions.D1: v3 expands execution and reproduction information: FP16, torch.profiler, FlashAttention except for ToCa, A6000 memory measurement, 5,000 MS-COCO images, explicit selection ratios, and configurations for new baselines and distilled-model integrations. These disclosures do not prove earlier settings differed. The front-page access pointer changes from a code repository to a project page, and the old custom-caching instructions disappear.
descriptions.R1: v3 adds context on Latent-SR and image-space super-resolution, forecasting methods, and token merging, alongside references supporting new metrics and implementations. FID and VQ4DiT references are removed. These additions refine the positioning, while the central distinction from training-dependent approaches and Bottleneck Sampling remains.
descriptions.P1: The title, abstract, introduction, artifact discussion, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. NT-DM is renamed NT-Matching, experiments gain dedicated artifact and edge-selection sections, and a Discussion section is introduced. Appendices are reorganized and references move after them, changing the narrative structure.
descriptions.P2: v3 switches to a two-column layout, redraws the framework diagram, merges the main benchmark tables, restructures integration displays, and adds quantitative artifact plots and appendix tables. Qualitative comparison panels and captions are revised. Some SD3 and FLUX 7× appendix images are retained and relocated, rather than newly added results.

P-4F5B4E3621.title: Quantifying Cross-Attention Interaction in Transformers for Interpreting TCR-pMHC Binding

descriptions.M1: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain identical query and key attribution procedures, pseudoinverse operations, and layer aggregation rules. The model-specific losses in Appendix A.4 and CLIP adaptation in Appendix A.12 are also unchanged.
descriptions.E1: Both versions use the same 274-complex TCR-XAI benchmark, VDJdb/IEDB/McPAS-TCR data, and 73,000-image MS-COCO subset. The new introduction reference to Appendix A.12 points to an existing vision-language experiment, not added coverage.
descriptions.E2: Section 4 retains AttnLRP, TokenTM, AttCAT, Rollout, GradCAM, LRP, and RawAttn. Comparator membership also remains unchanged within the integrated-dataset, runtime, ablation, and case-study comparisons.
descriptions.E3: Distance thresholds, importance-score smoothing, perturbation thresholds, BRHR evaluation, and confidence-based grouping remain unchanged. Appendix A.12 retains the 65,700/7,300 training/test split and 100 training epochs.
descriptions.E4: Both versions contain the same maximum-versus-average and cross-versus-self-attention ablations, threshold sensitivity studies, training-similarity and prediction-outcome analyses, and structural and CLIP case studies. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.
descriptions.E5: Tables 4 and 5 retain the same plus/minus and parenthesized variability reporting. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised.
descriptions.E6: Matched numerical entries and graphical findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains QCAI's CDR3b LOdds of -3.498 and AOPC of 0.045; Appendix A.12 retains 94.08% accuracy and 0.9997 ROC-AUC.
descriptions.T1: The attention definitions, pseudoinverse derivation, and aggregation equations in Sections 2–3 are unchanged, as are the BRHR definition and Appendix A.3.1 task formalization. No mathematical assumptions, proofs, or reasoning are added or corrected.
descriptions.C1: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion preserve the same contributions and performance claims concerning QCAI, TCR-XAI, and BRHR. The added Appendix A.12 pointer does not expand the applicability claim already supported and discussed in v2.
descriptions.C2: Both versions retain the same justification for physical distance as an importance proxy, interpretation of cross-attention's contribution, caveat about sequence changes affecting explanations, and future directions involving energy metrics and explain-by-design models.
descriptions.D1: Appendix B replaces the description of a supplied code package and planned public release with explicit project-website and GitHub source-code locations, also added to the main text. It removes the earlier weight-retrieval guidance and trained-weight release promise. Implementation and hardware details remain unchanged; trained-weight availability is not established.
descriptions.R1: The duplicate BERT preprint reference is consolidated into the retained publication, NetTCR-2.2 receives publication metadata, and the Vaswani author list is corrected. These concern the same cited works; the literature coverage and research positioning are unchanged.
descriptions.P1: v3 adds acknowledgments, code-availability text, and publication headers, alongside limited wording edits, an Appendix A.12 cross-reference, and bibliographic cleanup. The scientific narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.
descriptions.P2: The publication headers, title-page link, and added code and acknowledgment text cause limited reflow, including references spilling onto an additional page. All 14 figures and 13 tables retain their content, captions, and display structure.

P-A09F7DACFB.title: Segmentation-Guided Homography Estimation for Long-Term Planar Tracking

descriptions.M1: The described pipeline retains SAM2+ segmentation, Hough boundary fitting, DINOv2 symmetry disambiguation, reduced-degree-of-freedom handling of partial visibility, and WOFTSAM's tracking/re-detection/fallback cascade. Additional explanations, ablated variants and experiments do not establish a revised proposed algorithm.
descriptions.E1: v2 adds MPOT-3K evaluation alongside the retained POT-210 and PlanarTrack benchmarks, extending coverage to scenes containing multiple planar targets. Each object_id is tracked independently; this does not establish joint multiple-object tracking capability.
descriptions.E2: v2 Table S2 introduces minimum-area rectangle and Ramer-Douglas-Peucker mask-fitting baselines, plus SAM-H without DINO disambiguation. Section 4.1 also introduces a reported PRTrack comparison on MPOT-3K. Existing benchmark comparators remain; HVC-Net already participated in re-annotated PlanarTrack evaluation in v1 Figure S5.
descriptions.E3: The added MPOT-3K protocol tracks fixed object identities and reports p@50 alongside p@5/p@15, explicitly differing from PRTrack's Hungarian matching. New parameter sweeps and motion-only baseline controls extend the evaluation design. Appendix experiments use a newer computing stack; retained main benchmark settings are unchanged.
descriptions.E4: v2 adds symmetry-consistency sensitivity, DINO removal, Hough parameter sensitivity, simple mask-fitting comparisons, a WOFTSAM segmentation-variant test, and cascade usage/rescue/failure diagnostics. The existing inlier-threshold study moves from v1 Table S1 to v2 Table 5. Conversely, v1's detailed PlanarTrack threshold/attribute curves and attribute-combination analysis disappear; its mirror case study is relocated rather than newly added.
descriptions.E5: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, performance error bars or formal significance tests. New diagnostic percentages and results from a different computing stack do not introduce uncertainty estimation.
descriptions.E6: Headline POT-210 and PlanarTrack scores remain unchanged. v2 Table 2 adds MPOT-3K p@5/p@15/p@50 results: 67.0/89.9/95.1 for WOFTSAM and 54.2/81.2/89.9 for SAM-H. New ablation and cascade findings expand the results. Appendix SAM-H scores of 62.4/80.5 use a newer stack, so they are not same-setting gains over 62.0/80.1. v1's detailed PlanarTrack curves and 67.1 p@5 oracle entry are omitted.
descriptions.T1: Section 3 changes the explicit pre-warp equations to use inverse homographies where v1 used forward homographies, correcting the transformation direction. Other geometric definitions and Hough calculations are retained, with no new theorem or proof.
descriptions.C1: v2 explicitly foregrounds the training-free mask-to-homography formulation. It also corrects benchmark leadership claims: SAM-H leads PlanarTrack, while WOFTSAM leads POT-210 and exceeds prior PlanarTrack methods. v1's introduction and conclusion credited WOFTSAM with state-of-the-art performance on both.
descriptions.C2: v2 adds interpretations of the new ablations and cascade diagnostics, explicitly discusses failures of the inlier-ratio heuristic, and qualifies MPOT-3K evaluation through matching and annotation limitations. It removes detailed discussion of indistinguishable distractors, texture-based symmetry ambiguities and contextual reasoning. The central quadrilateral, occlusion and complementarity limitations remain.
descriptions.D1: v2 documents the new appendix experiments' A100/EPYC hardware and CUDA, cuDNN and PyTorch versions, plus per-frame RDP tuning and motion-only controls. Existing implementation and annotation instructions largely remain. Appendix B changes annotation-tool availability to a future release, conflicting with the retained publication claim in the conclusion; actual availability remains unresolved locally.
descriptions.R1: v2 adds and discusses the Multiple Planar Object Tracking work underlying PRTrack and MPOT-3K. It expands WOFT's description and emphasizes training-free geometric extraction from segmentation, while retaining most of the existing related-work coverage.
descriptions.P1: The title, abstract, introduction, method explanation, results narrative, limitations and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Experiments are reorganized into main results, ablations, computational efficiency and annotation quality, with corresponding appendix restructuring. This changes the narrative beyond simply inserting new experiments.
descriptions.P2: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation, with extensive float relocation and a redrawn cascade diagram. v1 Tables 2 and 3 are consolidated into v2 Table 1, and several experimental tables are added. Appendix examples move into the main text, while v1 Figures S5/S6 disappear. v2 Figure 10 redisplays an existing occlusion example.

P-8B0B3C4CD2.title: Residual Diffusion Bridge Model for Image Restoration

descriptions.M1: Algorithm 2 changes the t=T assignment from x_T=mu to x_{T-1}=mu, a limited revision to the specified sampling initialization. The residual modulation, bridge equations, training objective, and U-Net variants remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change or rerun.
descriptions.E1: The five restoration tasks, real-world generalization datasets, POLED/TOLED evaluation, and translation/inpainting coverage are retained. Appendix Table S1 lists the same datasets. The added efficiency measurements use resolution settings within retained image coverage.
descriptions.E2: The same 13 restoration comparators and six translation/inpainting comparators remain evaluated. Table S2 reuses the restoration comparator set. Newly cited FLAIR and ResFusion are not added as evaluated baselines.
descriptions.E3: New Table S2 evaluates memory, inference time, and FPS at 256x256, 512x512, and 1024x1024. Existing dataset counts, restoration metrics, training budgets, model configurations, and stated 10-step testing setting are unchanged.
descriptions.E4: Appendix H.5 adds an analysis of how computational cost scales with image resolution across RDBM variants and comparators. Existing noise-schedule, lambda, sampling-step, and residual-choice ablations, noise-map analyses, and qualitative cases are retained.
descriptions.E5: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new efficiency table likewise provides point estimates without introducing statistical reporting.
descriptions.E6: Table S2 adds computational results: for example, RDBM-L takes 0.504 seconds at 256x256 and 8.135 seconds at 1024x1024. Existing results in Tables 2-9 are unchanged, including RDBM-L's reported average PSNR/SSIM of 31.04/0.917 in Table 2.
descriptions.T1: Table 1 revises bridge specialization conditions, including VP lambda from infinity to 1/2 and Brownian bridge from lambda approaching 1/2 to 2*lambda*theta_t approaching 1. Appendix F.1 also changes the stated implied lambda from 1 to 1/2. The principal propositions and proofs remain.
descriptions.C1: The central claims of a unified bridge framework, residual-adaptive restoration, and superior empirical performance are retained. The revised conclusion explicitly mentions translation and inpainting, but these were already claimed and evaluated in v1.
descriptions.C2: New Appendix H.5 interprets RDBM as moderately efficient and balancing restoration performance against resource consumption. Existing explanations of sampling-step behavior and limitations concerning fixed lambda and distributions lacking correspondence remain unchanged.
descriptions.D1: Appendix H.5 newly states the mixed dataset's 256-to-1024-pixel resolution range. Appendix I adds a claim that supplementary code is provided and public release will follow camera-ready submission, conflicting with the retained abstract statement that code is already public. Actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.
descriptions.R1: v3 adds four cited works: FLAIR, ResFusion, a pan-sharpening unfolded-network paper, and Universal Pansharpening Foundation Model. These extend related-work coverage without changing the central positioning of RDBM.
descriptions.P1: v3 edits selected explanations and the conclusion, corrects 'Zero-Short' to 'Zero-Shot,' expands affiliations, adds acknowledgments, and removes the appendix contents page. Most prose and the main section organization remain intact.
descriptions.P2: v3 adds Table S2, tightens figure/table spacing, and corrects Figure 7's caption from TOLED generalization to image translation and inpainting. Existing empirical image panels and table structures are largely retained.

P-0DD59C002A.title: Retro-Expert: Collaborative Reasoning for Interpretable Retrosynthesis

descriptions.M1: v3 introduces Chem-RM's RDKit-based structural reward and a correction-weighted nonlinear advantage calculation for KGPO (Section 3.5). These revise reward modeling and optimization. Candidate selection, generation and rewards for rejecting incorrect candidates already appeared in v2, including its Figure 5.
descriptions.E1: USPTO-50K, USPTO-FULL, ChemBench, PaRoutes and the two wet-lab targets are retained. v3 Section 4.7 additionally reports testing 3-oxa[3.1.1]propellane and 3-aza[3.1.1]propellane as challenging targets beyond the benchmarks, providing a limited coverage extension.
descriptions.E2: v3 Table 1 adds Gemini-2.5-Pro, Claude-3-7-sonnet and Qwen few-shot/SFT comparison rows. Tables 2–3 add MHNReact and NAG2G. Conversely, the standalone DMS-Deep comparator in v2 Table 8 disappears from v3's multi-step comparison, although the same cited work remains the route generator under the name DMS-Model.
descriptions.E3: v3 introduces an expert evaluation of 500 samples across six annotation dimensions and matched-reward GRPO/KGPO controls. Multi-step evaluation adds success rate, Top-5 accuracy and inference time. T5Chem is newly evaluated with decision space, and the candidate-count sweep replaces N=7 with N=8. Dataset splits and the 9k/80k training subsets remain unchanged.
descriptions.E4: v3 adds reward-component and matched-optimizer ablations (Tables 7 and 16), candidate-use and rejection analyses (Tables 10–11), and reasoning correctness/consistency analyses. Appendix C adds route-combination case analysis. Existing decision-space, candidate-count and positional-bias analyses are retained; selection examples are revised and reduced, while generation and failure examples largely persist.
descriptions.E5: v2 reports averaged expert scores without agreement estimates. v3 adds unanimous and majority inter-annotator agreement, including 83% and 98% for reasoning faithfulness (Table 13), and examines unanimously rated cases. Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.
descriptions.E6: Reported Retro-Expert Top-1 accuracy changes from 70.28% to 75.69% on USPTO-50K, 49.3% to 58.4% on USPTO-FULL, and 57.00% to 65.67% on ChemBench. Explanation scores, ablation results and self-correction success also change. PaRoutes reports 41% versus v2's 38%, alongside new metrics and newly specified beam settings. These are results for the revised algorithm; wet-lab yields remain 79.3% and 58.82%.
descriptions.T1: v3 substantively expands the mathematical specification with a structural-feature reward, revised composite rewards, correction-weighted advantages and an explicit policy update (Section 3.5). Its reasoning trajectory also incorporates product-structure analysis and selectively used candidate dimensions. These exceed notation changes; neither version supplies theorems or proofs.
descriptions.C1: v3 withdraws v2's repeated claim to be the first retrosynthesis model generating natural-language reasoning. It refocuses the stated contributions on Chem-RM and the revised KGPO mechanism, and explicitly emphasizes efficient multi-step extension. The central interpretable collaborative-reasoning and model-compatibility claims remain.
descriptions.C2: Appendix I newly acknowledges chemically flawed rationales despite correct answers, limitations of the 7B backbone, and the preliminary nature of multi-step planning. v2's narrower site/path failure discussion is retained. v3 also interprets reasoning–answer alignment as causal evidence in Section 4.3, a stronger conclusion than the observational analyses establish.
descriptions.D1: v3 adds a source-code link, specifies multi-step beam size and route formatting, documents wet-lab case-selection criteria, and supplies revised reward weights. These extend reproducibility information, while the existing sample-curation procedure, core training configuration, prompts and detailed wet-lab procedures are largely retained.
descriptions.R1: v3 adds discussion or citations for Mol-R1, reward calibration, new comparators and propellane synthesis while retaining the related-work organization. It also replaces the chemical Retroformer reference by Wan et al. with Yao et al.'s differently titled language-agent Retroformer paper, despite retaining the numerical baseline.
descriptions.P1: The introduction and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten, including the exploration cold-start motivation. Interpretability evaluation is reorganized into reasoning reliability and explanation quality. The appendix is reordered into Sections A–I, moving existing evaluation material earlier and separating implementation, multi-step analysis, prompts and limitations.
descriptions.P2: v3 consolidates and expands the LLM comparison table, adds several analysis tables, redraws the reward diagram and adopts a largely single-column appendix layout. Spectra and existing examples are resized or relocated, and selection panels are replaced or removed. Caption errors are introduced: Figure 11 labels the retained deprotection example as oxidation.

P-2C047109C0.title: Lighting in Motion: Spatiotemporal HDR Lighting Estimation

descriptions.M1: The diffusion models, geometric conditioning maps, exposure prompts, mirror/diffuse predictions, and HDRI reconstruction procedure remain unchanged. Clarified descriptions and newly disclosed sphere-sizing information do not establish an algorithm change.
